_what_this_is: Hypothesis registry (Edge Playbook section 4.7). Every claim this project has tested, its status, and what would change the verdict. It exists because a killed idea has a habit of coming back wearing a new name — and because a project that only records its wins learns nothing. Status values: KILLED (evidence against, do not revive without the stated trigger), OPEN (running, insufficient evidence), CORRECTED (was believed, found wrong, fixed), PARKED (untested, blocked on something specific).
_rules: One observation per event. Wallets, markets and days are not interchangeable units.
A verdict needs the same statistical bar in both directions. Asymmetric gating manufactured a false INVERTED result once already.
Nothing is 'confirmed' by the run that generated the hypothesis. Reproduction or it did not happen.
Record the sample size that would settle it BEFORE looking at results.

confirmed.claim: The -4.39c hurdle is a property of the T-24h pre-game regime, not of the exchange. As settlement approaches and liquidity arrives, the cost of crossing falls.
confirmed.motivation: Live depth measurement 2026-08-13: the liquid core of Kalshi quotes a 1.0c median spread with a median 24,292 contracts at the ask and $46,628 within 2c; total 24h volume across real series is 26.5M contracts ($26.5M notional). H10's 'median size at bid FIVE contracts' and H46's sizes of 3.85-50.54 were correct and were taken on weather ladders and cross-listed macro contracts - the illiquid periphery.
confirmed.mechanism: The spread collapses from 5.01c at 24h to ~1.3c from 4h onward. The half-spread saving (1.82c) and the P&L improvement (1.87c) MATCH, so the gain passes through to the taker in full rather than being absorbed by adverse selection. That pass-through was the pre-registered check and is why the finding stands.
confirmed.robustness: Leave-one-series-out stable at every lead. Coverage 81-100%, never selection-contaminated. Not strictly monotone (4h beats 2h and 1h) but the 2h interval is wide and the shape is unambiguous.
confirmed.fee_correction: First study to use REAL per-series fee multipliers. KXMLBGAME is 0.5; every prior study including H56 assumed 1.0 everywhere. Correcting H56's 30 MLB events of 346 moves its headline about +0.09c, from -4.39c to approximately -4.30c. Immaterial, inside the interval, recorded for completeness.
confirmed.status: CONFIRMED. The cost of taking liquidity is horizon-dependent and roughly halves between 24 hours and 10 minutes before settlement. It is never positive at any horizon tested.

killed.claim: For cross-listed events the two venues' settlement CRITERIA diverge, so a cross-venue box does not pay exactly $1 — it can pay $2 or $0.

killed.it_corrects_H16: H16 killed cross-venue arbitrage on a 2.46c gap vs a 4.83c round trip. Its unstated premise was that exactly one leg pays. That is FALSE for 15 of 16 pairs — the trade is an unhedged bet on settlement criteria that looks riskless.
killed.the_one_sided_mechanism: Polymarket carries explicit fallback clauses (no-release, VP tiebreak, precedence, default-to-No) where Kalshi's rules_primary is a single silent sentence. Those fire by resolving Polymarket YES where Kalshi's silence leaves NO — the DIV-DOWN direction. The box is biased toward paying ZERO, so it is a trap and the correct direction is to SELL it.

Recession: Polymarket also resolves YES on an NBER declaration, which happened in 2001 and 2020 WITHOUT two negative quarters. CPI: if BLS never publishes July, Polymarket resolves on JUNE's number. Shutdown: Kalshi is a 10:00 ET snapshot, Polymarket any lapse by 23:59 — ~14 hours unmatched.
killed.status: KILLED as a trade; the classification stands as a correction to H16.

price_leg.the_prediction: If divergence is priced, DIV-DOWN boxes (which can pay ZERO) should cost LESS than $1 — you must be paid to hold them — and DIV-UP boxes (which can pay $2) should cost MORE.
price_leg.the_observation_is_exactly_backwards: Mean box cost by class: IDENTICAL 1.0110 (n=1), DIV-UP 0.9955 (n=2), DIV-DOWN 1.0246 (n=5), BOTH 1.0392 (n=6). DIV-DOWN costs MORE than a dollar and DIV-UP costs LESS — the reverse of the prediction on both sides.
price_leg.but_it_is_not_a_short_either: Every real box costs ABOVE $1.00 — all-divergent mean 1.0268, range 0.99 to 1.07 — so buying any of them loses before the divergence even matters. corrected.claim: Cohort labels in the boring-vs-news A/B are measured.
corrected.found: They were not, for one deploy. The house market list persists in KV, so after v11.1 shipped it still held pre-cohort entries with no cohort and no fee. The fill loop read `pos.cohort = mk.cohort || pos.cohort || 'news'` and labelled every one of them NEWS. Worse, the legacy verification sweep opens with `if (pos.cohort) continue`, so the invented label blocked the lookup that would have corrected it - a guess that defends itself from being checked.
corrected.how_found: Not by a test. By reading the live deploy's inventory table and noticing a confident cohort label sitting next to feeType 'unknown'. A measured label always brings its fee schedule with it; an invented one cannot.
corrected.impact: Caught within ~15 minutes of deploy, before the A/B had accumulated fills. Had it run, the news arm would have been contaminated with unlabelled markets and the boring-vs-news verdict would have been decided by a default.
corrected.fix: Default is now 'unverified', which has its own markout bucket the comparison never reads; verification re-asks anything 'unverified'; and a market list lacking cohort/fee forces an immediate refresh instead of waiting up to an hour for the cadence. Regression test wtest15 includes the starved-refresh path, since the obvious version of the test passes even with the bug present.
corrected.lesson: Three of this project's worst bugs now share one shape: a fallback that invents a value rather than admitting it does not have one. Fills counted as positions, winnerIndex defaulting to 1, and now cohort defaulting to news. The fix is always the same - carry 'unknown' as a first-class value and let it be visibly absent.

method_rules_added.rule: Measure the price you could have TRANSACTED at, not the price you observed.
method_rules_added.test: For any entry taken from a bar, re-run the identical strategy entering one bar later. If the edge does not survive one bar of delay it is a measurement of the past, not an opportunity. A bar's closing price is unknowable until the bar closes, so acting on it is lookahead by construction.
method_rules_added.why: H61 passed unit-of-observation, event bootstrap, leave-one-series-out, concentration, coverage, specification AND out-of-sample replication to within 0.03c, and was still worth nothing. None of those checks asks whether the price was obtainable.

mechanisms_added: Where the price is attractive, the market is not there - now four independent routes. Far-OTM tails carry no bid (H34), cheap rungs never win (H53), near-certainties are not quoted at the horizon you would enter (H55), and short-horizon favourites reprice away faster than a polling architecture can act (H61).

The cost of crossing is a FUNCTION of horizon, not a constant. It halves between 24 hours and 10 minutes as the spread collapses from 5.01c to ~1.3c, and the saving passes through to the taker in full (H60).
Fee schedules vary by instrument. KXMLBGAME carries fee_multiplier 0.5 where the code assumed 1.0 everywhere. Read the multiplier, never assume it.

state_of_play_2026_08_10.the_hurdle: -4.03c per contract, 95% CI [-7.4, -0.7], on 41 independent settled events. The cost of crossing the spread, and the number every future idea must beat.
the_mechanisms: Taker on public info: edge = spread + fee; the public feed is 78-258s behind a book that moves at 180s.
Maker capturing spread: the spread IS the compensation for adverse selection.
Maker collecting a subsidy: the reward is tied quadratically to exposure.
Internal-consistency arb: the two books are one book; ladders are monotone; sets sum to $1.
Cross-venue: gap < round trip — and per H46 it was never even a hedge.
Model vs market: the free model's error bar is WIDER than the market's implied distribution (4 instances).
Long-dated tails: collateral drag beats mispricing; a 6000x mispricing returns 0.91%/yr.
Short-dated tails: where the tick exceeds fair value the book is empty.
Every bias measurable from free data is a bias only relative to free data.
Prices are calibrated on both venues at every bucket with enough events to test.
Spread and flow are inversely coupled — no market offers both.

Cross-venue boxes: settlement criteria diverge on 15 of 16 cross-listed pairs, and the market prices the box at ~$1 regardless — so the criteria risk is real, unpriced, and still unharvestable, because the box costs above a dollar before the divergence matters.
Rulebook breadth IS priced: on strict-superset pairs the broader contract is dearer by ~0.39c on average, the correct sign. What looked unpriced in the box was the two round trips.
Non-partition ladders: where no exclusivity clause exists, multiple legs can pay, and the market already prices it — mids sum to 110c where a partition caps at 100c.

Path, not level: hourly changes mean-revert at -0.247 lag-1, interval excluding zero and robust across six specifications. Expected reversion 0.17c against a 2.00c spread — 11.7x against. The only significant effect found, and still sub-spread.

Reversion in the quote path is real and does not reach the fill economics.
